builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
summary: SkillEarth replaces manually authored tool-call prompts, predefined expert knowledge, and parameter retraining with reusable skill files automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories and refined through real tool-chain execution feedback plus a dual-judge routing graph. The cost is added pipeline complexity: trajectory collection, execution-grounded refinement loops, judge model calls, and a skill retrieval and versioning layer that must be maintained in production. It can fail if extracted skills overfit to demonstrated trajectories and misroute on novel tasks, if judge feedback encodes errors into skills, or if the remote-sensing results do not transfer to the reader's tool domain.
rationale: The pattern of externalizing tool-call knowledge as retrievable, retraining-free skill files is adoptable on constrained infrastructure via API-based LLMs, but the evidence is confined to remote-sensing benchmarks without quantified deltas, so it warrants a small workload-specific pilot rather than direct production adoption.
technique: Self-evolving tool-call skill extraction and retrieval

claims.statement: SkillEarth replaces manually authored tool-call prompts, predefined expert knowledge, and parameter retraining with reusable skill files automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories and refined through real tool-chain execution feedback plus a dual-judge routing graph. The cost is added pipeline complexity: trajectory collection, execution-grounded refinement loops, judge model calls, and a skill retrieval and versioning layer that must be maintained in production. It can fail if extracted skills overfit to demonstrated trajectories and misroute on novel tasks, if judge feedback encodes errors into skills, or if the remote-sensing results do not transfer to the reader's tool domain.

The abstract claims improved tool selection, argument correctness, execution-order consistency, and task completion over existing RS agents and skill extraction methods on OpenEarth-Bench and Earth-Bench, across three frontier and four open-source LLMs, but provides no quantified figures.
